# team-comms.md templates

## Contents

- [Template 1 — Claude Code host](#template-1--claude-code-host)
- [Template 2 — GitHub Copilot host](#template-2--github-copilot-host)

Scout writes `.agents/team-comms.md` during project seeding. The content
depends on the detected host. Pick the matching template below, substitute
the enumerated roster, and write the file.

**Every generated `team-comms.md` must start with this header:**

```markdown
<!-- GENERATED BY SCOUT — DO NOT EDIT. Re-run scout to refresh. -->
```

The header is load-bearing: it tells readers (and future scout runs) that
the file is owned by the seeder and overwritten on every seed. Hand edits
will be lost.

Two templates follow, in order:

1. Claude Code host
2. GitHub Copilot host

Multi-host projects (e.g. both Claude Code and Copilot installed)
concatenate templates 1 and 2 into a single file, with a one-line note at
the top telling each runtime which section applies.

---

## Template 1 — Claude Code host

```markdown
<!-- GENERATED BY SCOUT — DO NOT EDIT. Re-run scout to refresh. -->

# Team Communication

> Generated by scout on <YYYY-MM-DD>.

## Setup

- **Host:** Claude Code (`.claude/agents/`).
- **Dispatch:** your host's subagent tool, by roster name. Prose never dispatches.
- **Installed personas:** <N> — see the roster below.

## Team roster

| Role | `subagent_type` | Hand off… |
|------|-----------------|-----------|
<!-- one row per .claude/agents/ subdirectory, from AGENT.md name + description — co-installed factories' personas (e.g. manual-qa's test-runner) get rows too -->
| Test Automation Lead (orchestrator) | `test-automation-lead` | Pipeline routing, dispatch, merge gate |
| Test Automation Engineer | `test-automation-engineer` | Automation implementation, review slot |
| Scout | `scout` | Codebase onboarding, re-discovery |

Use the `subagent_type` value exactly — it must match a directory name in
`.claude/agents/`.

## How to hand off work

Dispatch is **one call to your host's subagent tool** — the tool in your list
that launches a named agent with a prompt. Pass the roster name exactly as the
agent file's frontmatter `name:` spells it, a 3–5-word description, and a
self-contained prompt. The call blocks; the subagent's final message comes
back as the tool result in the same turn. There is no queue, no background
mode and no notification.

Two things never dispatch: prose ("use the engineer agent to …" — the runtime
does not read your reply for instructions) and a call written as text in some
other host's syntax. Nothing needs enabling in any agent file: never add
`tools:` or `agents:` to make dispatch work.

**One subagent** — one call. **Several** — several calls in the same reply,
only for read-only work on a finished diff (reviewers); nothing that writes
runs concurrently, one working tree has one state at a time.

## When to hand off vs. do it yourself

| Situation | Hand off? |
|---|---|
| Need a result to continue (engineer builds the spec → reviewer verdicts → gate) | **Yes — subagent** |
| Parallel independent work | **Yes — multiple subagents in one turn** |
| Quick research / investigation / planning by another persona | **Yes** |
| Small task clearly inside your own role | **No — just do it** |
| Fire-and-forget | **Not an option** — no queue, call and wait |
| Multi-turn back-and-forth with the subagent | **No** — split into one-shot calls with full context each time |

## Writing prompts for subagents

1. **State the goal.** What outcome do you want back?
2. **Give the context.** File paths, excerpts, originating request, prior
   decisions. Paste the text — don't just reference it.
3. **Set the constraints.** Format, length, scope, what *not* to do.
4. **Bound the response.** "Report in under 200 words." "Return Gherkin
   only." "List files as a bullet list with one-line annotations."

Terse prompts produce shallow, generic work. Be specific or don't hand
off.

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hand off trivially.** One grep and one edit away? Do it.
- **Don't hand off to a persona not in the roster above.** It's a hard
  error — check the roster first.
- **Don't hand off and discard.** The subagent's result belongs in your
  reply. Silent discards are lost work.
- **Don't try to simulate async.** There is no queue. Call, wait, continue.

## Reporting back to your caller

The subagent's result is yours to integrate — don't narrate the tool
calls, show the outcome. After a hand-off, summarize what each subagent
produced, show the concrete deliverable, and call out blockers and next
steps in the same reply.
```

```markdown
# Team Communication

> Generated by scout on <YYYY-MM-DD>.

## Setup

- **Host:** GitHub Copilot (`.github/agents/`).
- **Dispatch:** your host's subagent tool, by roster name. Prose never dispatches.
- **Installed personas:** <N> — see the roster below.

## Team roster

| Role | Copilot agent name | Hand off… |
|------|--------------------|-----------|
<!-- one row per .github/agents/ entry, from the agent file's frontmatter name + description — co-installed factories' personas (e.g. manual-qa's test-runner) get rows too -->
| Test Automation Lead (orchestrator) | `test-automation-lead` | Pipeline routing, dispatch, merge gate |
| Test Automation Engineer | `test-automation-engineer` | Automation implementation, review slot |
| Scout | `scout` | Codebase onboarding, re-discovery |

Use the agent name exactly as it appears in the file's YAML frontmatter.

## How to hand off work

Dispatch is **one call to your host's subagent tool** — the tool in your list
that launches a named agent with a prompt. Pass the roster name exactly as the
agent file's frontmatter `name:` spells it, a 3–5-word description, and a
self-contained prompt. The call blocks; the subagent's final message comes

mode and no notification.

**One subagent** — one call. **Several** — several calls in the same reply,
only for read-only work on a finished diff (reviewers); nothing that writes
runs concurrently, one working tree has one state at a time.

## When to hand off vs. do it yourself

| Situation | Hand off? |
|---|---|
| Need a result to continue (engineer builds the spec → reviewer verdicts → gate) | **Yes — subagent** |
| Parallel independent work | **Yes — list multiple in the same reply** |
| Quick research / investigation / planning by another persona | **Yes** |
| Small task clearly inside your own role | **No — just do it** |
| Fire-and-forget | **Not an option** — no queue, call and wait |
| Multi-turn back-and-forth with the subagent | **No** — split into one-shot calls with full context each time |

## Writing prompts for subagents

1. **State the goal.** What outcome do you want back?
2. **Give the context.** File paths, excerpts, originating request, prior

3. **Set the constraints.** Format, length, scope, what *not* to do.
4. **Bound the response.** "Report in under 200 words." "Return Gherkin

Terse prompts produce shallow, generic work. Be specific or don't hand
off.

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hand off trivially.** One grep and one edit away? Do it.
- **Don't write a dispatch as text.** Only a call to your subagent tool
  runs anything; prose and pasted syntax from another host both print and
  do nothing.
- **Don't edit agent frontmatter to "enable" dispatch.** Nothing needs
  enabling; a `tools:` key can only take tools away.
- **Don't confuse `handoffs:` with in-run subagent calls.** `handoffs:`
  is post-run navigation; subagent calls are mid-run delegation.
- **Don't hand off and discard.** The subagent's result belongs in your
  reply.

## Reporting back to your caller

The subagent's result is yours to integrate — don't narrate the tool
calls, show the outcome. After a hand-off, summarize what each subagent
produced, show the concrete deliverable, and call out blockers and next
steps in the same reply.
```
